record.original_question: Let F = {a1(t), ..., aℓ(t)} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth. Is the family of integer sequences {[a1(n)], ..., [aℓ(n)]} good for ℓ-convergence of a single transformation exactly when every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) either stays farther than logarithmic scale from every real multiple of an integer polynomial, or differs from some real multiple of an integer polynomial by a finite limit, or stays within O(log t) of t/m for some nonzero integer m?

evidence.quote: Problem 22. Let F be as above. Show that the family of sequences {([a1(n)]), . . . , ([aℓ(n)])} is good for ℓ-convergence of a single transformation if and only if every function a ∈ span∗(F) satisfies one of the following conditions: • |a(t) − cp(t)|/ log t → ∞ for every c ∈ R and p ∈ Z[t]; or • a(t) − cp(t) → d for some c, d ∈ R; or • |a(t) − t/m| ≤ C log t for some non-zero m ∈ Z and C > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a Hardy field, i.e. a field (under pointwise operations) of germs at $+\infty$ of real-valued functions defined on half-lines $[t_0,\infty)$, closed under differentiation. A function $a\in\mathcal{H}$ is said to have polynomial growth if there exists an integer $k\ge 0$ with $|a(t)|/t^k\to 0$ as $t\to\infty$. Fix $\ell\ge 1$ and let $F=\{a_1,\dots,a_\ell\}\subset\mathcal{H}$ consist of functions of polynomial growth. Write $\operatorname{span}^*(F)$ for the set of nonzero real linear combinations $c_1 a_1+\cdots+c_\ell a_\ell$.

For a measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ on a probability space and $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, consider the averages
$$A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell):=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} T^{\lfloor a_1(n)\rfloor}f_1\cdot T^{\lfloor a_2(n)\rfloor}f_2\cdots T^{\lfloor a_\ell(n)\rfloor}f_\ell.$$
Call the family $\{(\lfloor a_1(n)\rfloor),\dots,(\lfloor a_\ell(n)\rfloor)\}$ \emph{good for $\ell$-convergence of a single transformation} if for every such system and every choice of $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages $A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell)$ converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N\to\infty$.

Prove or disprove: $\{(\lfloor a_1(n)\rfloor),\dots,(\lfloor a_\ell(n)\rfloor)\}$ is good for $\ell$-convergence of a single transformation if and only if every $a\in\operatorname{span}^*(F)$ satisfies at least one of the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item $|a(t)-c\,p(t)|/\log t\to\infty$ as $t\to\infty$ for every $c\in\mathbb{R}$ and every $p\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$; or
\item $a(t)-c\,p(t)\to d$ as $t\to\infty$ for some $c,d\in\mathbb{R}$ and some $p\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$; or
\item $|a(t)-t/m|\le C\log t$ for all sufficiently large $t$, for some nonzero $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ and some $C>0$.
\end{itemize}
artifact.category_tag: Ergodic averages along Hardy field sequences
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: Tsinas (arXiv:2109.07941) and Frantzikinakis–Tsinas (arXiv:2006.03558) established mean convergence of such multiple ergodic averages for Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth under the "logarithmic independence" condition (the first bullet), confirming several conjectures of Frantzikinakis. The full equivalence with the three-case characterization has not been fully verified in the surveyed literature, so the problem appears partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Joint ergodicity of Hardy field sequences
status_evidence.snippet: if all non-trivial linear combinations stay logarithmically away from rational polynomials, then the L^2 limit of ergodic averages exists and equals the product of integrals, establishing a conjecture of Frantzikinakis.
status_evidence.claim: Partial confirmation of the conjectured criterion under the first (logarithmic) condition.

status_evidence.title: Multiple ergodic averages along functions from a Hardy field: convergence, recurrence and combinatorial applications
status_evidence.snippet: Confirms some of the conjectures posed by Frantzikinakis on convergence and recurrence of multiple ergodic averages along functions from a Hardy field.
status_evidence.claim: Progress toward, but not full resolution of, the proposed if-and-only-if criterion.
